Setting up an alternative, more open distribution, as well as an alternate desktop environment experiment. Also checking to see how dwm and void and worst of all nvidia, will behave in a different setup.
Maybe a fallback, maybe not.
⬛️ initial install Alright so during the initial install from the base iso (extremely minimal) a couple of things of notice:
EFI needs 1G, setup as EFI boot, vfat, MOUNT at /boot/efi / is required, ext4 /home can be separate, ext4 If GRUB crashes at the end of the installation it’s probably due to some mismatch in the initial installation where it doesn’t see/find the steps it needs to install. If all is setup correctly (and secureboot etc hasn’t messed something up) chroot and grub-install MIGHT be a solution. ⚫️ we have the user, the admin, and a tty alright so here, after updates and **xbps** has been updated too we got the terminal and basically nothing besides bash. before we get to dwm, need a few things:
xinit, xorgminimal, xauth sudo xbps-install -S xorg-minimal xauth xinit
xorg fonts, and a video driver to be updated with nvidia instructions (soon tm) sudo xbps-install -S xorg-fonts font-misc-misc xf86-video-vesa
After these, we got most stuff, time to get to the dwm things. This dwm install is based through FAUN-Dev Community guide on medium, link at the end.
Void packages (case sensitive):
sudo xbps-install base-devel libX11-devel libXft-devel libXinerama-devel freetype-devel fontconfig-devel Might as well grab micro here:
sudo xbps-install micro step 1: clone
mkdir .suckless cd .suckless grab dwm (provisional until personal repo/config is up)
git clone https://git.suckless.org/dwm git clone https://git.suckless.org/st git clone https://git.suckless.org/dmenu step 2: compile
cd .suckless cd dwm make sudo make clean install cd.. cd st make sudo make clean install cd .. cd dmenu make sudo make clean install` cd step 3: starting
If you’re using startx, simply add exec /usr/local/bin/dwm at the end of your .xinitrc file on Linux, or at the end of your .xsession file on OpenBSD.
touch ~/.xinitrc echo "exec dwm" > ~/.xinitrc startx should now get into dwm, shift+alt+enter: st terminal, shift+alt+q: exit dwm (provisional until customized) Good luck!
links https://archive.is/dD9qc www.suckless.org https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l-f5KgibVfI penguin (good) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7l9AuRU9ax4&t=112s

The maps in this section were produced within the hour of data acquisition or news development, reference graphics intended to place a story quickly, not exhaustive analyses.
South Georgia, US Active fire detection Source: NASA FIRMS / LANCE — 26 April 2026
The Highway 82 and Pineland Road fires broke out in southeastern Georgia on 20 April, driven by extreme drought, high winds, and debris left by Hurricane Helene. By the 26th, the two fires had together burned over 50,000 acres and destroyed more than 120 homes.
This map uses FIRMS/LANCE near-real-time active fire detection data from 26 April, showing hotspot positions across Brantley and Clinch counties at the time of acquisition. The FIRMS is sub-daily detection. Really important for mapping active fronts. (Highway 82 fire doubled in size overnight)
The map was produced and published the same day as data acquisition, as part of a response to the State of Emergency declared by Governor Kemp across 91 counties on 22 April.
Update — 28 April: the Pineland Road fire had reached 32,000 acres at 23% containment; Highway 82 22,600 acres at 32% containment. Rain over the weekend provided temporary relief but conditions remain dry. The burn ban across 91 counties remains in effect.
Active fire detection: landscape true color Source: NASA FIRMS / LANCE, true color base — 26 April 2026
This map overlays FIRMS hotspot detections on a true color base layer, showing active fire positions across Brantley and Clinch counties against the wider landscape context. The two smoke plumes tracking northeast are clearly visible, consistent with the wind direction driving both fires during this period. The Atlantic coastline is visible to the east, placing the fires roughly 50 miles inland.
The true color base gives a clearer read of the smoke extent and direction than a processed composite would at this scale, and confirms the separation between the two fire fronts at the time of acquisition.
Mourne Mountains, Northern Ireland Active fire detection Source: NASA FIRMS / LANCE — 26 April 2026
Two significant wildfires broke out across the Mourne Mountains in County Down, requiring a major response from the Northern Ireland Fire and Rescue Service. The fires occurred across upland terrain, where access is difficult and wind exposure accelerates spread.
This map uses FIRMS/LANCE near-real-time hotspot detection from 26 April, placing the active fire positions within the wider Mourne landscape and relative to Belfast.
Update — 29 April: NIFRS confirmed one of the two major incidents had been successfully resolved. A second substantial blaze remains active with crews on scene.
Burn extent Source: Sentinel-2 MSI — 26 April 2026
The second map in this pair uses Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery from 26 April to show the spatial extent of the affected area across the Mournes. Also it shows the active fire fronts, and burn scar, as well as the smoke plume.
Update — 29 April: situation ongoing. No structural damage or casualties reported in coverage to date.
DRC — Current state Sources: IPIS Research, ACLED, Critical Threats Project, OCHA, OHCHR, UN Group of Experts (July 2025), Sentinel-2 imagery (Copernicus). As of April 2026.
The left panel shows the extent of active conflict and M23/Rwanda-controlled territory across Ituri, Nord-Kivu, and Sud-Kivu as of April 2026, against the ceasefire lines nominally agreed in the Luanda process. The right panel breaks down control and influence by actor: M23/Rwanda in teal across the Kivu corridor, with contested and FDLR-influenced areas in purple across Ituri and the northern fringe. The grey areas indicate zones where armed group presence is documented but control is disputed or fragmented. The gap between the two panels is the story: the ceasefire exists on paper across most of this territory while the ground situation reflects continued consolidation along the Rwanda border corridor.
Update — 29 April: situation ongoing

Toggle the slowdown scenario to see the modelled annual mean cooling at major North Atlantic and Nordic cities under a full AMOC shutdown.
The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is the system of currents that carries warm water from the tropics to the North Atlantic and returns cold water south at depth. It is part of the reason northwestern Europe is warmer than its latitude would suggest. A study published in Science Advances in April 2026 (Portmann et al.) found that observational constraints project a roughly 51% AMOC weakening by 2100 under a moderate emissions scenario — sharper than previous model estimates. A companion paper (van Westen et al., 2025) reports observational evidence consistent with this trajectory. The map below shows the warm surface flow on top, the cold deep return below, and the three sites where surface water cools, becomes denser, and sinks — driving the whole circulation.

Evros ABSS Summary The Evros Automated Border Surveillance System (ABSS) is a permanent, fixed-location layer of the border security apparatus. Its coverage ranged from the river Delta, all the way to the north tri-border near the city of Orestiada. I geolocated the nodes of this network through satellite imagery, public tenders, and various press articles and photographs.
Detailed Methodology The Evros border has been a testing ground and a funnel for a host of EU-wide research (CERETAB, AIDERS και ROBORDER and projects employing those) into surveillance and machine vision which involves a wide arrange of stakeholders from across different law enforcement and research centers in the EU. A lot of this is showcased during the Greek Ministry of Migration’s presentation of the REACTION program. The autonomous surveillance systems presented show their applications in urban environments with identification of people and vehicles and “total monitoring” of set areas. They are created to be deployed in ad-hoc scenarios by staff on the ground.
ABSS Tender The Automated Border Surveillance System (ABSS) is a permanent, fixed-location additional layer of the border security apparatus alongside the fence, the increasingly militarized (including new military-issue patrol vehicles up to deploying confiscated MRAPs for patrol purposes) and technologically upgraded police/ border guard patrols, and various other actions (including the expansion of the anti-armor trench between the two countries alongside increased army presence, to the militias being formed by locals and donations of thermal cameras to army units, heartbeat sensors at checkpoints, etc).
The projects presented and listed are sponsored through a combination of EU and GR funding. The EU funding for research is from the Horizon2020 as well as case by case border reinforcement programs. The funding split ranged from 75% to 90% of EU funds.
In 2016, the Hellenic Police initiates a public tender for “Expansion of the automated border surveillance system in the river area of the Hellenic-Turkish border at the Evros area and the interconnection of the Regional Centers for Integrated Border Management and Migration (RCIBMM (PEKODISME in Greek))” The 14.9 million euros were 75% funded by the Internal Security Fund (ISF) of the Directorate-General for Migration and Home Affairs of the European Commission (DG HOME).
Documents link1:16122016-diakir.pdf /broken link link2: Ω3ΓΧ465ΦΘΕ-ΤΚ3.pdf /broken link
The project was undertaken by Space Hellas S.A. (GR) and OTE S.A. (GR).
On the 20th of October 2021, mainstream media in Greece reported that the system, which they dubbed the “electronic shield of Evros” had started its trial phase, and would be in full operation a month later in November. The system is reported to cover the Evros border completely, from the mouth of the river delta, all the way up to the village of Sofiko, close to the city of Orestiada.
Mainstream reporting shows the pylons being put up as well as some imagery of the local centers / camera control rooms.
Newspaper / kathimerini.gr
Open channel
The pylons where the system was built on, were largely purpose-built. With some already existing infrastructure, mostly belonging to OTE S.A., were used especially for parts of the network that would function as relays or local control centers (without camera equipment). Due to the pylons being owned and administered by the Ministry of Citizen Protection they were exempted from being registered on the directory of high-powered communications antennae, where the rest of the pylons and antennae can be found. Owing to them also being classified as national security assets they were additionally exempt from any natural environment laws and protections (for example being built deep into Natura2000 areas).
Antennae information in Greece is publicly available here where one can search for them by municipality/general area or by map pin.
Antennae Network Despite that, the tender document contained some initial information regarding the specifications:
5 Pylons under the Orestiada Police Directorate supervision (ΟΣ*) 5 Pylons under the Alexandroupolis Police Directorate supervision (ΑΣ*) 1 Intermediate Broadcast station (ΒΣΤΔ1) 2 Regional Centers (Alexandroupolis and Orestiada) 4 Local Centers (Soufli, Tychero, Feres, Didymoteicho) Although the locations were not specified, either due to how early in the process this tender was drafted or due to security reasons, they create an initial impression of how the network is structured. Further in the document we find more information regarding the structure. This gives some insight into the trunk and branches. Much of the specification is there for the purpose of showing a basic structure and intent with further elaboration and details during the final design phase after the contract has been awarded.
In the same document, a larger scope of the network could be found as a diagram below. The red dashed line represents the main trunk and the purple line the secondary networks that feed into the connection points into the main. Mapping the network The diagram above was the starting point to create the network map. I already knew the location of the Alexandroupolis and Orestiada Regional centers.
According to the specifications as well as published material we knew that the local centers were to be found in the Border Guard/Police stations in the smaller towns.
Along the, now known, centers/nodes of the network, the tender’s provisional planning also included specification (as distance between each in meters) for the wireless high-powered coupling between the antennae themselves and then to the primary/trunk network.
Through these point to point distances between the nodes, some of them were already known which allowed for verification of the distances. At the same time it showed that the specified distances were not completely accurate. Probably due to deviations during the final planning and further changes during the construction phase.
Some minor deviations in distance, especially in cases where the building complexes were spaced far enough apart, were ignored. (The Didymoteicho police academy and the Feres/Poros border guard stations are examples of this). There has also been reporting that places the Regional Center of Alexandroupolis at the city’s airport, this was also ignored in favor of the specification that sees the receivers placed on top of the Police Directorate’s building. Based on this, I began identifying and placing these points on the composite map of Evros I created. (The network line at the southern edge, points towards the Police Headquarters in Athens were image is simultaneously broadcasted.)
The placement employed a variety of OSINT methods (like social media posts by activists, mainstream media, government announcements and photographs, satellite imagery).
Before and after imagery the pylons being installed: AS3 (ΑΣ3) near Lagyna AS5 (ΑΣ5) near Gemisti AS8 (ΑΣ8) river Delta AS10 (ΑΣ10) river Delta mouth * AS11 (ΑΣ11) near Monastiraki In the case of AS11, a before and after much like the rest of the pylons could not be determined by satellite. The location of an already installed pylon by the companies that were the primary contractors was chosen due to its location being one of the very few places where the coupling distances could situate it. The exact location might be a different one.
OS4 (ΟΣ4) near Sofiko OS5 (ΟΣ5) near Pythio OS6 (ΟΣ6) near Pythio OS7 (ΟΣ7) near Amorio OS8 (ΟΣ8) near Mandra Determination of range Another factor that assisted in the placement of the pylons beyond the distance between known points, the elevation, and the corresponding local and regional center, was the range of equipment mounted on those platforms.
The initial tender specifies for each, a thermal camera, a surface radar, and a laser rangefinder.
This factor defined any disputed location because the range of the thermal camera had to be able to reach the river and the border. (and in many cases penetrate quite far in both the Turkish and the Greek mainland)
The next step was to match and visualize the maximum range that the pylons would be able to monitor and look for humans.
This resulted in the following:
Showcasing that since its trial run in 2021 the system could provide nearly total coverage of the river Evros and the border area, sometimes stretching far inland. Due to the morphology of the river floodplain and the elevated position of the surveillance equipment it can be inferred that the thermal cameras can have a view of human activity in the area. This is also supplemented by the automatic detection software also specified.
Furthermore the equipment was specified to have a very high degree of freedom covering both horizontal and vertical angles.
These are the thermal cameras and radar on the pylons. They sometimes vary in placement where they might be hanging on the side of the pylon (and thus have less horizontal rotational freedom).
Smaller Scale Surveillance Equipment Manned guard posts along the river (from the second phase of the river fence expansion) as well as the army posts are equipped with cameras and thermal cameras in order to assist with the monitoring.
These while providing information to law enforcement are not interconnected with the larger ABSS network. In addition to the guard posts, the patrol network is providing another layer, this time of human, surveillance which is further assisted by drones operating on an ad-hoc basis.
This is also a focus of the research being conducted through the programs detailed at the start of the document. Related Media MRAP vehicle - Militarized border guard force.
Fence/deterrent gate detail.
Turkish surveillance camera, seen from the Greek side as the fence/deterrent is being constructed.
The pylon in the Delta (AS10) - center of the image.

content: ⬛️ links and before we begin https://github.com/EpicGames/UnrealEngine?tab=readme-ov-file#getting-up-and-running https://www.sidefx.com/forum/topic/61839/?page=1#post-404735 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TOpdnwBxEq4 (unlisted video, for UE4, but helpful stuff, sourcing houdini environment (the most useful part) at around 27:40) during houdini installation, choose the plugins you’ll want / need, otherwise install those now for the version you’re on (a lot of the time, the most recent bleeding edge version won’t play well with compiling alongside UE) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=600RgBneV_A (newer video, Manjaro base, UE5.1) ⬛️ First things make the directory for UE5 and switch to it git clone git@github.com:EpicGames/UnrealEngine.git now in the UE5 directory ./Setup.sh then find the plugin for unreal at /opt/sidefx/houdini_engine (you need to plugin that corresponds to the current version of houdini in the system, if you remove that version it will break the integration) get the HoudiniEngine folder and copy it in the Plugins/Runtime folder of UE5 NOW it is important to initialize the houdini environment before the next step so that when the make files are generated it knows what to look for cd /opt/hfsX source houdini_setup The Houdini 20.0.653 environment has been initialized. back in the top directory ./GenerateProjectFiles.sh [With the environment initialized you shouldn’t get any errors at the generate script] make (it shouldn’t require sudo) a lot of the times there might be some error in the UE make that just reks all of it. That’s 99% the houdini engine plugin. 1st try removing it from the directory and recompiling, it should go faster and without errors. Then is the troubleshooting, have to find a houdini version that UE5 agrees with and wants to compile. So off you go! after compiling has finished, and all has gone well, need shortcuts for rofi now ⬛️ regarding updates and changes soon(TM)

While using linux for vfx work I’ve had to do some general maintenance stuff, wrote the steps so that I understand the process better myself. I use linux mint btw.
⬛️ Moving /home (and some partitioning that was needed) This guide is the source of what I did: https://forums.linuxmint.com/viewtopic.php?p=2192189#p2192189 It’s written by a well respected member of the linux mint forums (rene, thank you), it’s really solid.
The guide being solid is no substitute to having backups and timeshifts, so do those. Using pika lately and really liking it. restart (or shutdown+power up again) and don’t login at the login screen Ctrl+Alt+F1 to bring up the console login as root, or use sudo before the commands run mount /dev/nameofyourdisk /mnt run df to check if the correct partition is mounted copy your home directory with rsycn -av /home/ /mnt/ (this will take some time, and a lot of weirdness on the screen if your home is quite big also make sure before you run this that it’s the correct drive with the correct mount) after this finishes run rm -r /home then run mkdir /home alternatively you can do mv /home /home.old && mkdir /home do a blkid to find your partition’s UUID, note it down and run nano /etc/fstab add a line with UUID (code) /home ext4 defaults 0 2 umount /mnt && mount /home (no output here is success) df to verify mount exit the console Ctrl+Alt+F7 to return to the graphical login In my case the mounting went weird (and the editing of the fstab part) because it kept erroring out because home remained mounted. I rebooted, started from a live Mint image, edited the fstab and rebooted and the system worked! ⚫️ Creating the partition on the disk that is both filesystem and /home currently. In my case, I had a whole nvme, where I'd thrown everything in (assigning /home to a separate partition is easier to do during the initial format) so in order to partition you can’t do it on a live system (and Gparted live PLEASE NO)
rebooted with a Mint installation media started Gparted found out I need to remove quite a few files from the current /home so that I could reduce it to a reasonable number (can’t partition lower than the current occupied space) offloaded files restarted the process and created a partition I labelled home, ext4 like my file system label helped with identifying it at the blkid list. waited for the whole thing to finish and started the process above Good luck!
links https://easylinuxtipsproject.blogspot.com/p/1.html

⬛️ Stubborn, non matching layer interpolation Alright, two layers (states) with different point count, different everything which resemble the state of an event days apart. Interpolation and fruffy stuff that creates curves and other weird gradient shit doesn't work. So: Create two tables (decimal(real) number type), let’s call them “Midpoint_X” , and “Midpoint_Y” those will be midpoint of the position between the coordinates of two points WHERE IT CAN FIND THEM AND WHERE THEY MAKE SENSE OTHERWISE WILL NEED CORRECTIONS DOWN THE LINE then you need to average the distance from your layer to the other, code below: (x($geometry) + x(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 (y($geometry) + y(geometry(get_feature('OTHERLAYER', 'fid', $id)))) / 2 that should be run to update the respective fields/tables.
Ok now we got points. Those will require inspection to see where they have ended up, as well as corrections. For static features, they should not have ever been interpolated so they can just be deleted. For moving features such as the fire progression for example it is a matter of determining which points to keep and which to throw away. These points can be used for PointsToPaths. [Optionally Clean them] Then split the paths. Explode them as well. (usually just the explodey part is enough) Happy times of manually cleaning weird geo (vertex tool + delete paths-lines) If it doesn’t commit the changes to the shapefile, export as Dissolve (error logs here, will help with identifying the element and removing it before moving to the next step) Test lines to polygons. If the polygon shaped makes sense, save it and move on. If it doesn’t geo probably needs more fixing. ⚫️ Attribute to geo for things like the circles of range etc
create the attribute and assign values per point (if not available) use Geometry by expression and having the layer with the info selected use: make_circle($geometry,r_VALUE*2,segments=36) if required split the geo into separate shapes for further use / port 🔶️ Add specific point Ok, this is easy :P (quite handy for documenting events that the coordinates are known, point by point and are developing live instead of being an easily created/accessible csv, or for comparisons) make_point("X", "Y") x=lat, y=lon keep in mind the coordinate system
bonus line between points that share the same id:
make_line(make_point("X", "Y"), geometry(get_feature('LAYERNAME', 'fid', $id))) this gets quite unstable when, you guessed it, have non-equal point count to match ids ◻️ Add the points’ coordinates as an actual attribute (for further use) Create the fields for x=lat, y=lon Initially those will have to be for EPSG:4326.
x(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) y(transform($geometry, layer_property(@layer, 'crs'),'EPSG:4326')) update the respective field for each 🗨️ Display bubbles in GIS, html for mouseover display This displays information based on the exported file + folder with material + material id in the csv on mouseover. <span style="font-weight:bolder;">[%"desc"%]</span></br> <img src="file:///[%@project_home%]/test/[%"img_id"%]" width="500" /> Also, specifying a type, which in my case I call (Cd) as well for further use, allows for per category labelling of the same layer.
🏔️ GIS DEM Generation / fix for displacement map soon (TM) Links:
https://vvzen.github.io/houdini/dem https://somethingaboutmaps.wordpress.com/blender-relief-tutorial-getting-set-up/
